Lion's schemas are refinement types checked while a program runs: they accept or refuse a value and never change it
Lion reads a recursive schema as its least fixed point, as the paper reads a positive inductive type
Every check of a recursive Lion schema ends, since the docs say a value fits only when that follows in finitely many steps
Lion's schemas and rules follow one rule for recursion through not
Lion has no function extensionality, so the inconsistency Liquid Haskell and F* met cannot arise in it

lion has: schema checks that never change the value they check
schemas that never change what a program computes
recursive schemas read as least fixed points
recursive schemas whose every check ends
schemas that recurse through not on a smaller part of the value
rules that recurse through not on a smaller argument
